name: Mashrabiya Wood
description: Traditional Egyptian lattice woodwork, carved from reclaimed acacia or cedar. Light golden-brown, often used for window screens and room dividers.
culturalNote: Mashrabiya screens filter desert light while maintaining privacy — a defining element of Islamic architecture since the Fatimid period.

name: Nile Limestone
description: Fine-grained limestone quarried from Nile Valley pits. Creamy beige with subtle fossil striations, the signature material of ancient Egyptian monuments.
culturalNote: Tura limestone was quarried for the faces of the Great Sphinx — its pure white surface was visible from Memphis 3,000 years ago.

name: Red Aswan Granite
description: Coarse-grained granodiorite from Aswan quarries. Deep red-garnet speckled with black mica — the stone of pharaonic obelisks and temple columns.
culturalNote: Aswan granite formed the cores of the pyramids at Giza. This stone has been quarried continuously for 5,000 years.

name: Carrara-Style Marble
description: Egyptian-produced marble matching Carrara aesthetic. Pure white with gray veining — the luxury surface for contemporary villas and hotel lobbies.
culturalNote: Egyptian Carrara marble offers the same luminosity as Italian Carrara at 40% lower cost, sourced from quarries near Luxor.

name: Egyptian Cotton Damask
description: Handwoven linen-cotton blend damask from Upper Egyptian villages. Geometric Islamic patterns woven with extra-long-staple GIZA cotton.
culturalNote: Egyptian damask weaving traditions date to the Fatimid period (10th century). Giza long-staple cotton produces fibers 2x longer than standard cotton.
